pr_title: SVGLoader:  Update vertices according uv.y when linecap is square

issue_context.title: SVGLoader pointsToStroke incorrect result using linecap square
issue_context.body:
### Description

When passing a simple 2 point line shape to SVGLoader pointToStroke, when linecap is set to square, the resulting geometry is incorrect.  

![image](https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/assets/25032599/4ec74360-8fbe-48ba-899b-bcb465e4ea25)

It works correctly when linecap is either butt or round.

### Reproduction steps

create a 2 point line shape
getStrokeStyle passing linecap set to 'square'
pass resulting shape and stroke style to pointsToStroke

### Code

```js
const shape = new Shape();
  shape.moveTo(-12, 0);
  shape.lineTo(12, 0);

  const style = SVGLoader.getStrokeStyle(
    2,
    "white",
    undefined,
    "square",
    undefined
  );

  const geometry = SVGLoader.pointsToStroke(shape.getPoints(), style);
  const material = new MeshBasicMaterial({ side: DoubleSide });
  const rect = new Mesh(geometry, material);
  scene.add(rect);
```


### Live example

https://codesandbox.io/s/three-stroke-square-test-3yn756

### Screenshots

![image](https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/assets/25032599/a3c2d140-c143-498b-8a3f-436fff193d9e)


### Version

156.1

### Device

Desktop

### Browser

Edge

### OS

Windows
comments: When I rotate the scene (using orbit), the missing triangle is facing backwards.  So likely the normal is just wrong or not being calculated.

review_comments:
The PR indeed fixes the issue and I don't see any regressions in `webgl_loader_svg`.

Do you mind explaining the reasoning behind this change though? Why does the code have to make a distinction at this line?

`tempV2_3` and `tempV2_4` are the two new vertices after the cap is calculated. They should replace the corresponding old vertices. Updates to `tempV2_3` and `tempV2_4` are explicit. But there are two cases of updating vertices[3] with `tempV2_3` or `tempV2_4`. `uv.y` is used to determine whether to use `tempV2_3` or `tempV2_4`.
It would be better if there was no need to make a distinction. Maybe there's a better way?
Not sure. If somebody comes up with a uniform approach, we can sill update the code. For now, let's go with the this PR.
